newsitem.title: USA: Comair, Delta off after crash.
newsitem.headline: Comair, Delta off after crash.

text.p: Comair Holdings Inc shares traded lower Friday in a pattern that typically follows an airline crash, analysts said.

"Typically, stocks, after a crash, tend to trade off a bit, then they bounce back," unless an airline has been negligent in maintenance, which has not been indicated in early investigation of the fatal crash Thursday of Comair's flight 3272 near Detroit, said an analyst who asked not to be named.
Comair shares fell 2-3/4 to 22-1/4 at midday on Nasdaq.
Delta Air Lines Inc, which Comair's website said owns about 20 percent of Comair, was off 1 to 71-1/4 on the New York Exchange. Comair is a feeder airline in the Delta system.

The analyst said he does not expect long-term impact on Delta, but Mark Koprucki, analyst at Ohio Co, said if the crash fuels concern about turboprop airplanes, Delta, whose feeder airlines operate such planes, could suffer.

On Comair, Koprucki said, "This is not meant to sound heartless to the families of the victims because it's certainly a terrible tragedy, (but) ...this momentary weakness in share price probably offers long-term investors a buying opportunity." He expects Comair to continue growing, adding it has an excellent safety record and stresses safety above all.
Early investigation of the crash had not yet determined a cause. The region had been hit by a snowstorm but there was no confirmation that weather was a factor.
